chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, then what?' So he said: 'I do not assert to you that He, the Exalted, will create a creation who will worship Him.'
ai.seo_question: What happens after Paradise and Hell are filled according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the state of existence after the final entry of Paradise and Hell dwellings, suggesting that Allah may create new beings for worship. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of Allah’s absolute power to create anew, emphasizing that divine worship is an eternal attribute not confined to the current cosmic order. The narration underscores the continuity of servitude and adoration in the post-resurrection reality, aligning with the concept of *khalk jadid* (new creation).

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 18.Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a)

whom he asked, “When Allah admits the inhabitants of Paradise into Paradise and the inmates of Hell into Hell, then what?” So he said, “I do not make the assertion to you that He, the Exalted, will [surely] create another creation who will worship Him [but if He wills, He may do so].”
